# NewModularProduct — Overall Activity Plan and Status

**Status date:** 30 September 2026  
**Current verified baseline:** 31 passing tests, 0 failures (`node --test`)  
**Latest committed workflow checkpoint:** `f8ccd33 feat: compose pure application preparation workflow`

## Delivery roadmap

| # | Activity | Goal / deliverable | Status | Evidence / notes |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Establish safe migration boundary | Use sanitized legacy source only; exclude secrets, actual CVs, local configuration, generated outputs, outreach, UI, and integrations from the first slices | Complete | Migration work used focused source/test inspection and synthetic fixtures only |
| 1 | Discover verified legacy contracts | Extract behavior from source and Node tests for parser, ATS scoring, CV selection, path selection, and cover-letter generation | Complete | Replaced earlier inferred summaries with direct source/test-backed contracts |
| 2 | Set up modular Node project | Create ESM project, Node test command, source/test layout, Git hygiene, ignore rules, line-ending policy | Complete | `package.json`, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`; `node --test` |
| 3 | Implement shared text primitives | Provide normalization, tokenization, uniqueness, and overlap operations | Complete | `src/domain/shared/text-normalization.js` |
| 4 | Implement JD parsing | Convert raw job text into structured role, keywords, methods, location, domain, seniority, and clearance signals | Complete | `parseJobDescription()` plus contract tests |
| 5 | Implement ATS assessment | Score an in-memory CV against a parsed JD and return explanation components/suggestions | Complete | `scoreCvAgainstJd()` plus scoring tests |
| 6 | Implement CV ranking and best/alternative selection | Rank candidates and return a recommendation | Complete | `rankCvCandidates()` and `selectCv()`; preferred-code tie-breaker corrected intentionally |
| 7 | Implement selected-path candidate policy | Narrow inventory by path identifiers and synthesize metadata for unknown selected identifiers without I/O | Complete | `selectCvsByPath()`; Windows path semantics are explicit and tested |
| 8 | Implement cover-letter domain | Fill templates, validate output, generate draft, clean citation markers, add ATS paragraph, and highlight terms | Complete | Explicit template required; candidate details supplied as inputs rather than hard-coded |
| 9 | Compose pure application workflow | Provide a single in-memory operation from JD input to CV recommendation and validated cover letter | Complete | `prepareApplication()` plus two end-to-end synthetic tests |
| 10 | Write/update architecture documentation | Maintain high-level/low-level design, diagrams, contracts, boundaries, and roadmap | Complete, needs small refresh | Markdown document exists; update baseline from 29 to 31 tests and mark `prepareApplication` implemented |
| 11 | Add JSON CLI interface | Read one JSON request from stdin; run application workflow; emit one JSON result to stdout; report errors to stderr | Ready to start | Design and code plan prepared; not yet implemented or tested |
| 12 | Validate CLI end-to-end | Add CLI command tests and a synthetic stdin/stdout smoke test | Not started | Target after Activity 11: 36 tests total expected |
| 13 | Commit CLI checkpoint | Commit only CLI adapter, CLI tests, and package script change | Not started | Planned commit: `feat: add JSON application preparation CLI` |
| 14 | Define infrastructure ports | Specify stable interfaces for template storage, CV inventory, and document text extraction | Planned | Must stay outside `src/domain` |
| 15 | Add template-loading adapter | Load an explicit named template from a controlled source and pass it to pure application workflow | Planned | Prefer this before CV document ingestion |
| 16 | Add CV inventory adapter | Load candidate metadata from an approved storage format and map it to domain input shape | Planned | No real personal data until privacy/storage policy is decided |
| 17 | Add document text extraction adapter | Extract text from approved CV documents with error handling, path validation, and optional caching | Planned | Requires careful sensitive-data handling; do not put in domain |
| 18 | Add a human-facing interface | Choose CLI enhancements, HTTP API, or web UI after the JSON boundary is stable | Planned | Interface should call application services, never domain internals directly |
| 19 | Add optional external research/refinement ports | Integrate company research or LLM refinement through explicit interfaces and audit/error controls | Deferred | Requires explicit provider, privacy, cost, and secret-management design |
| 20 | Add outreach/email only with safety design | Create drafts/queues first; require explicit confirmation before any send operation | Deferred | Separate high-risk slice; credentials, consent, recipient resolution, and audit trail required |

## Current architecture state

```text
Implemented and tested

Job-description text
  → parseJobDescription
  → selectCvsByPath (optional path subset)
  → scoreCvAgainstJd
  → rankCvCandidates / selectCv
  → generateCoverLetter / validateCoverLetter
  → prepareApplication

Next boundary

JSON stdin
  → CLI adapter
  → prepareApplication
  → JSON stdout
```

## Completed checkpoints

| Commit | Checkpoint |
|---|---|
| `aa70cce` | Pure JD parsing and CV ranking core |
| `694f7eb` | `.gitignore` protection |
| `bdd32a1` | Text-file line-ending policy |
| `7a2fdb1` | Pure CV selection policy |
| `48fff66` | CV path selection policy |
| `f8ccd33` | Pure application preparation workflow |
| Cover-letter checkpoint | Implemented and tested; verify its exact commit hash locally if needed |

## Decision gates

1. **Before Activity 11:** Confirm the architecture document is refreshed to the 31-test baseline.
2. **Before Activities 14–17:** Decide where candidate data may be stored, who can access it, and whether it may contain sensitive personal information.
3. **Before Activity 19:** Select providers and define data minimization, cost limits, retry behavior, logging, and secret storage.
4. **Before Activity 20:** Require a separate communication-safety design with explicit human approval for every send action.

## Recommended immediate next action

Implement **Activity 11: JSON CLI interface**, then run its command tests and a synthetic stdin/stdout smoke test. This makes the completed pure workflow usable without widening the trust boundary.

## Milestone reconciliation - 10 October 2026

This section supersedes the earlier current-baseline, executive-status,
and immediate-next-action statements. The original capability plan and
implementation order remain in effect.

### Delivered since the original baseline

- JSON application-preparation CLI and command tests.
- Controlled template and JSON CV inventory adapters.
- Local PDF text extraction; full indexing/cache is not confirmed complete.
- Local HTTP application preparation and interactive review interface.
- Organisation research through an explicit Perplexity adapter.
- Cover-letter refinement proposals with explicit user acceptance.
- Contact import, persistence, linking, unlinking, and deletion workflows.
- Per-import business-domain selection in LinkedIn userscript version 0.4.1.

### Latest completed checkpoint

- Commit: 4f45966 - Move LinkedIn userscript and replace hardcoded import domain.
- Live validation: version 0.4.1, entered ageas.co.uk, generated candidate
  nico.detullio@ageas.co.uk, no reported error.
- This validates candidate-domain handling, not mailbox verification.
- Agreed repository cleanup checkpoint is closed.
- Last reported test baseline: 239 Node tests and 14 browser tests passing.
  These tests were not rerun for this documentation update.

### Outstanding and deferred scope

- Automated recruiter discovery/ranking is not established as delivered.
- Recruiter TSV/export and reviewable outreach preparation remain the next
  planned delivery area, subject to checking existing implementation.
- Older-duplicate review-domain projection remains deferred unless it blocks
  the next delivery.
- Full CV indexing/cache, CV rebuilding, and persistent application output
  are not established as complete.
- Gmail OAuth, draft creation, and sending remain deferred behind Phase D gates.

### Delivery focus

Follow the existing roadmap. Deliver the smallest useful vertical slice,
use focused validation, and record status/evidence at each milestone.
Do not reopen cleanup or add speculative refactoring as prerequisites.

Next delivery slice: persistent local outreach queue from selected linked
contacts, with explicit recipient selection and message review. Gmail draft
creation follows, then explicitly approved sending. TSV export is optional.

## Current reconciliation — 15 October 2026

This dated section supersedes earlier current-status, test-baseline and next-action
statements, including the 10 October reconciliation. Historical sections remain
as the record of earlier milestones; this does not renumber the original plans.

### Evidence boundary

- Source snapshot: codebase-checkpoint-audit-20261014T231729786588Z.txt.
- Captured branch/HEAD: feat/review-provider-output / 2e12757. This is the audit
  reference, not a claim that a new checkpoint commit has been created.
- Existing focused tests and user-reported small live flows are distinct evidence.
  The user reported working draft/send flows and two-email batches; larger-volume
  behaviour and automatic uncertain-outcome reconciliation are not established.
- No fresh full-project test baseline is asserted here. Earlier 29/31/239 Node and
  14-browser counts are historical, not a current full-suite execution report.
- Legacy advert normalization is present in the source. A source audit alone does
  not confirm repair of existing database rows or the resulting Gmail draft.

### Delivered implementation

The application is no longer only an in-memory core. It includes the deterministic
JD/ATS/CV/letter core, JSON CLI, controlled template/inventory adapters, local PDF
extraction, HTTP review UI, organisation research, accepted refinement proposals,
contact import/linking/domain handling, persistent outreach, OAuth mailbox checking,
reviewed draft creation, explicit sending, recorded history and small bulk workflows.
Durable application-review storage and Save/resume controls are wired in startup;
live restart/resume validation remains separate from source presence. Inferred
contact email candidates are not verified mailboxes.

### Architecture at this checkpoint

Interfaces (CLI/HTTP/browser) call application services; the deterministic domain
remains separate from file/database/provider adapters. Durable application reviews,
contact/domain persistence, outreach queue and draft/send ledgers are distinct stores.
The Python Gmail workers form an external-effect boundary. Keep credentials and
private runtime data outside source control. Preserve exact-content confirmation,
CV-byte checks, version checks and uncertain-operation locks. Editing local source,
restoring it from Git, or saving an application must not reset a mail ledger or replay
an external operation. This reconciliation is not a complete architecture/security
sign-off or confirmation that every original requirement is finished.

### Remaining formal migration scope

Numbers here refer to NewModularProduct-Full-Migration-Plan.md, not the shorter
Overall Activity Plan, whose activity numbering is different.

- Area 11: PDF extraction exists; full fingerprinted indexing/cache remains open.
- Area 12: CV rebuilding remains a separate outstanding workflow.
- Areas 18–19: imported contacts/domain candidates do not establish automated
  recruiter discovery or ranking as delivered.
- Area 21: TSV export is optional/unverified; it does not block the working queue.
- Areas 22–25: Gmail/outreach implementation and limited live validation exist;
  large batches and automatic uncertain-outcome recovery are not signed off.
- Area 26: current persistence is not a complete freshness/TTL/retention policy.
- Area 27: durable reviews exist; application-file export/user-selected output
  handling and live restart/resume evidence remain distinct outstanding work.
- Areas 28–30: configuration/events exist; privacy, retention, security and recovery
  requirements still need explicit review rather than blanket completion claims.

### Checkpoint and next delivery

Create a reviewed WIP source/test checkpoint with its actual validation limitations.
Keep the 55 captured tracked utility deletions outside the feature checkpoint unless
separately approved. Keep both Playwright configs and the repair utility imported by
the normalization tests. Preserve local rollback packages. Do not broadly stage,
clean or delete untracked files; new runtime modules are among them.

The default Playwright config can reuse the normal server on port 3000. Full browser
regression must use a dedicated fixture server, temporary data and fake/disabled live
integrations. A different port alone does not isolate hard-coded runtime paths.

Next useful delivery is the unfinished export part of area 27: explicitly download
the reviewed letter as TXT/HTML, optionally with the selected existing CV, using safe
filenames. No CV rewriting, paid request or Gmail action is part of that export.
Interview/follow-up tracking is optional enhancement, not a new mandatory migration
prerequisite. Do not reopen broad cleanup or speculative refactoring to block usage.

# NewModularProduct — continuation checkpoint and roadmap priorities

Checkpoint date: 21 October 2026
Purpose: persist locally and use as handoff context for a future development session.

## Current operating boundary

- Development: `D:\monorepo\NewModularProduct`, loopback port 3000, started via the existing `start-local-server.bat`.
- Production: `D:\NewModularProduct-Production`, loopback port 3100. It restarted successfully after a stale supervisor lock caused by the user-reported abrupt laptop shutdown. The root cause is plausible, not proven. The user removed the stale lock only after read-only inspection showed old supervisor/Node PIDs were absent, no listener existed on 3100 and the status heartbeat was over eleven hours old.
- Production must not be stopped or changed during normal development checks. Never delete supervisor locks without checking process/status/port first.
- Existing private scheduler authorisation and its private sheet are configured under a dedicated OAuth project. Existing reports showed `configured:true`, the sheet ID `1lcVbf1GQhJlrYU4eQGab_2YRrv7aU1ZnXiHOVn71SHw`, namespace `4be96a87-1bd4-cb7a-4bc8-a09b3ade5f06`, and local scheduling flag false. Do not reauthorise or recreate it.
- Never request/share `.env`, OAuth client JSON/tokens, actual CVs or databases. No assistant-run live Gmail, Google, ATS or production action has occurred.
- User prefers a focused, consolidated bundle and speed after essential checks; avoid gold-plating or many partial patches.

## Source/artifact continuity

- Only complete uploaded source snapshot available: `next-slice-source-20261019T185518217479Z.json`, 263 files, source HEAD `1c641c44ca711cd76713fd1de9f01c132c45b3dd`.
- Its contents were source-captured and hash-checked in prior sessions. Do not call it a live checkout, current Git tree, or the user's post-install state.
- Development CV/Word rebuild bundle: `development-rebuild-CV-Word-v1.zip`. User ran installer `--check`; it reported 518 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip application tests and 83/83 Python tests, then user confirmed `--apply` reported `APPLICATION INTELLIGENCE DEVELOPMENT SOURCES APPLIED` and started development. The confirmed installation is the cumulative CV/Word rebuild plus the earlier firstname-export hotfix, installed before the later application-intelligence bundle.
- The 1 skipped app test should be identified before production promotion; never count it as a pass.
- The next `application-intelligence-MVP-development-v1.zip` was delivered, but user has NOT confirmed that it was checked/applied. Assume the history/assessment panel and new `application-intelligence-v1.db` are NOT installed until the user reports otherwise.
- The earlier candidate source notebooks/files were ephemeral and no longer exist in the current tool session. Do not assert those exact worktrees are available.

## User-confirmed runtime observations

- The user explicitly confirmed the actual selected `Vijay Dafal_ProgMgr.pdf` preview showed correct Programme Manager CV text and the exact-original download opened the correct PDF.
- After the firstname-export update, the user reported the ZIP export downloaded. Immediately before the later grouped-history work, they still reported this error when exporting: “Saved plain and formatted letter disagree. Save/review the letter again. Queue/Gmail unchanged.”
- Investigation reproduced the parity failure: the saved letter had `I am applying for the [role](advert URL)` in rich HTML while plain text also retained `Role details: <advert URL>`. `restoreLinkedOpeningPlain` normalises this case for Gmail/send validation, but the exporter only handled an advert-only standalone paragraph. A precise export fix was designed in an isolated ephemeral source tree and 12 targeted checks passed, but the source/artifact was lost. The durable rebuild bundle does NOT include that fix. Rebuild it from current live source, ensure only the approved exact link/role representation is normalised for comparison, and ensure exported/stored letter bytes remain unchanged. Do not weaken real content divergence checks.

## Most recent grouped-history state — NOT INSTALLED

User asked to group the many sends shown separately under paired address variants. The user output showed, for one Relief International LinkedIn vacancy, many pairs such as first.last@ri.org and last.first@ri.org, with 125 legacy operation records lacking robust vacancy metadata. This is strong evidence of UX/contact grouping need, NOT proof paired addresses are the same verified contact.

Design/evolving prototype:
- Group by exact stable vacancy/application key + normalized contact identity (prefer fullName; address fallback) for presentation only.
- Preserve each send row, every address, action, timestamp and exact Gmail message ID. Warn for alternate addresses; label inferred/manual/unknown address source and verification separately. Never auto-merge/delete/verify addresses.
- Keep different vacancies separate. Missing identity remains separate/unknown rather than guessed. Similarity/alternate identity must never silently become an exact match.
- Existing API `items` compatibility should remain; add per-send contact/vacancy `groups` and paginate consistently. Search should filter send records before grouping. Do not return full message body.
- No schema migration, send-path change, Gmail operation or mutation of history.
- 19 focused renderer/API/queue/SQLite tests were reported passing in prior temporary work; full application suite 490/490 passed only after restoring the missing test helper and test-only versioned template. The full queue browser module did not mount in a synthetic harness; later isolated renderer/browser testing used a static fixture. The candidate is not packaged or installed.
- The previous temporary renderer fake-DOM suite had iterations where test doubles lacked `replaceChildren`, table-header/body, or textContent behaviour. Do not claim a failing run passed. In future, use `jsdom`/the existing Playwright browser if available, or faithfully implement DOM semantics. No Chromium server connection is proof of UI integration unless the actual queue root and module mount.
- A later dedicated static fixture/server attempt also had a harness-root/port problem and did not establish the actual full application queue mount. This remains an explicit acceptance gate, not a finished browser integration.

## Application Intelligence MVP notes — development bundle delivered, install unconfirmed

Requirements were requested and written to `Application-History-and-CV-Learning-Roadmap.md` in tool output, but that roadmap file/source is not necessarily present in the current user's checkout. The separate dev source bundle `application-intelligence-MVP-development-v1.zip` has not been confirmed applied.

Intended MVP:
- Prior activity check against saved review/queue/draft/confirmed-send/manual external submission records; never claim inbox/portal audit.
- Distinguish saved/prepared, queued/drafted/scheduled, confirmed outreach vs user-recorded external submission. An email send is NOT proof of ATS submission. “No match in stored records” is not “never applied.”
- Exact vacancy identity by stable source job ID, advertiser-scoped reference, canonical URL with only known tracking parameters removed; possible repost/similarity stays advisory. Cross recruiter recipient variants should find exact vacancy history.
- User-confirmed external submission entry with source/provenance/idempotency, and non-destructive void correction.
- Versioned assessment snapshots: CV role/file hash/text hash, JD hash, assessment/scoring scheme, complete requirement coverage/gaps, extraction warning. Do NOT store full CV/JD text in the history DB or sheet. Legacy score is separate.
- Current MVP “literal keyword coverage” is not employer ATS score, semantic fit, skill proof, or interview probability. Unavailable extraction is `unavailable/null`, never score 0 or metadata fallback.
- Separate local `application-intelligence-v1.db`, explicit schema guard and development-only initialization. Production database migration/backup contract not included. Test installer check/apply against exact current local source first.
- User's previous installation report did not include this feature bundle, so assume absent.

## Highest-value remaining work (recommended order)

1. Close the observed export plain/HTML parity bug with a surgical, fully tested source patch.
2. Finish grouped-history browser integration as an optional high-value UX fix after acceptance; no store rewrite.
3. Inspect the current 3000 dev checkout changes/source guards and establish which bundles are actually installed. Re-run preflight only after that evidence.
4. Application Intelligence MVP install/verify on dev 3000, if its bundle is current and hash check passes. Test history search against the user's actual existing records locally; don't ask them to upload records.
5. Role-family recurring gap dashboard, with complete assessed requirement counts, denominators and immutable versioned CV/JD/scorer snapshots.
6. Evidence-led SMART achievement rewrite proposals: source-backed evidence, user-reviewed; missing metrics/timeframes remain missing; no fabricated targets/results.
7. Recruiter search links: user-requested manual, user-clicked LinkedIn search URLs only. Expose title/company/location query variants (e.g. Director, Head, Talent), open the LinkedIn People search page, no scraping/bots/profile extraction or automatic email inference. LinkedIn prohibits unauthorized automation/scraping; user controls search/results and explicit contact selection.
8. Apps Script scheduling work stays a separate high-risk track; not enabled. Complete live per-file permission, signature, crash/cancel race and rollback acceptance before enabling any trigger.
9. Don't enable or test live Gmail sending as part of these slices. Existing per-message explicit confirmation remains.

## What to ask the user for before resuming

- Confirm whether `application-intelligence-MVP-development-v1.zip` was run on `--check` and `--apply`; if yes, share only safe summary/errors, not data.
- For export parity, ask them to confirm exact non-sensitive shape only: is the advert URL repeated in a “Role details” plain line, or is there another rich-vs-plain difference? No CV/letter body required.
- Do not ask to repeatedly rerun Google OAuth, recreate the sheet, share client credentials or modify the `.env`.

## Claims that are not justified

- No current live source tree or actual CV/JD/recruiter/email database was inspected by the assistant.
- The broad original full-product roadmap is not complete. CV/Word development is confirmed installed; scheduler, SMART, history-group browser/package and prior-application bundle status remain as documented above.
- Browser acceptance of the grouped-history patch is not complete; do not say that it is.
- No production promotion, Google worker installation, scheduling trigger creation, email send or rollback occurred in these assistant sessions.

# Development roadmap: next application slices

Status: PLANNED — no application, database or production changes applied by this document.
Operating model: development on port 3000; production on port 3100 remains usable. Promote only an explicitly reviewed and tested commit. Do not reseed production data.

## Delivery policy

- Deliver two coherent development packages rather than a sequence of ad hoc UI patches.
- Each package includes complete affected files, related automated tests, installation/verification instructions, backup/rollback instructions, and a roadmap status update.
- Use one current development-source snapshot for each package; do not assume older uploads are unchanged.
- Work on development only. Existing production configuration, credentials, saved applications, contacts, queued snapshots, drafts and sent history must not be overwritten.
- Do not silently enable Gmail or change production feature flags during UI work.
- No new deployment mechanism, vector database or background paid-processing pipeline is required for these slices.

## Slice 1 — Evidence-led application preparation

### 1. Preferred CV role codes

Expose all supported codes from the configured CV inventory as searchable multi-select options showing both code and readable role name. Do not invent unsupported codes or imply a corresponding CV exists. Preserve existing saved preferences and the distinction between preferred codes and the one selected attachment.

### 2. Achievement checkbox selector

Replace free-text CV Highlights for new preparation flows with selectable evidence-backed achievements. Preserve existing saved free-text highlights as legacy application evidence rather than deleting or silently reinterpreting them.

Workflow:
1. Read the selected CV and any explicitly approved career evidence.
2. Produce candidate achievement statements grounded in those sources.
3. Show result, personal contribution/how, supported metric, timeframe and source attribution.
4. Let the user inspect the evidence and select the statements to include.
5. Compose the default cover letter from the selections.
6. Pass selections and their evidence to Perplexity only after the user requests polishing and confirms the existing cost step.

Statement template, not a candidate fact:
Delivered [documented result] by [documented actions or methods], within [documented timeframe].

Evidence rules:
- Every material claim must link to its source passage and source version/hash.
- Keep employer, role/engagement, timeframe, achievement and personal contribution together.
- Do not borrow a portfolio metric for an individual engagement without explicit source support.
- Do not treat an employment period as proof of a delivery deadline or time-to-result.
- Do not invent targets, percentages, dates, savings, budgets, team sizes or causal explanations to fill SMART fields.
- Qualitative supported outcomes remain usable, but must not be labelled fully SMART when measurement/time evidence is absent.
- Unsupported proposed details remain unselectable until supported by evidence or explicitly verified by the user.
- Keep team outcomes distinct from the candidate's personal contribution.
- Suggestions may be ranked for JD relevance, but not silently selected or sent.
- No paid model call on page load, checkbox changes, CV changes, model changes or tone changes.

Persistence:
Store selected achievement IDs plus approved wording and evidence-version snapshots with the application where possible. Revalidate selections when the selected CV changes. Changes to an evidence catalogue must not rewrite saved letters or existing queue snapshots. Keep private evidence outside Git and release source archives.

### 3. Preparation layout

Place job title, organisation/advertiser name and job location in a responsive three-column row on wide screens. Stack naturally on narrow screens and preserve full editable values.

### 4. Job poster details

Display imported poster name, supplied headline and safe profile link in the relevant section. Do not infer a poster, infer an email, auto-import a contact, queue a message or send anything merely because a poster is present.

### Slice 1 acceptance

- Supported CV codes load from inventory and existing selections survive save/resume.
- Selected achievements survive reload and reach the default letter and polishing request with matching evidence.
- Invented metrics/timeframes/causation are rejected or marked unsupported.
- CV switching cannot silently reassign a claim to another engagement.
- Existing applications and queue snapshots remain unchanged.
- Preparation remains usable on wide and narrow viewports.
- Extraction/selection does not trigger a paid or Gmail action.

## Slice 2 — Application review workspace and selection controls

- Add a floating left-side section navigator with small icons, accessible names, keyboard navigation, active-section indication and no overlap with content. Collapse appropriately on narrow screens.
- Rearrange Vacancy details into a compact responsive grid.
- Place Email domain immediately after Vacancy details, alongside it on wide screens and underneath on narrow screens. Keep one authoritative domain field/state.
- Put Save application and Delete application next to each other. Preserve separate handlers, deletion confirmation and revision checks.
- Put rating/ATS summary elements in one compact desktop line, with responsive wrapping.
- Replace the polishing-model dropdown with visible single-select choice cards. Set the catalogue entry labelled GPT-6 Luna as the default for NEW applications; retain saved applications' existing selections. Validate the real provider ID against the application's catalogue.
- Replace the tone dropdown with visible single-select choice cards. Preserve saved choices.
- Use checkbox-like visual cards if desired, but native radio semantics for a single model/tone per request. True multi-model comparison is out of scope and requires a separate explicit cost/behaviour design.
- Keep genuine checkboxes for achievements and preferred role-code multi-selection.
- Move Unlink selected and Clear linked contacts above the Linked Contacts table.
- Move the existing below-table actions above Available imported contacts.
- Rearrange Imported LinkedIn advert into a responsive information grid, with expandable full description and poster details where supplied. Preserve captured content and provenance.
- Give Recorded sent history subject the flexible column width; compact other fields and keep technical details expandable. Prefer a single subject line on wide screens, while retaining full text and a usable overflow/expansion path for exceptional lengths and narrow screens.

### Slice 2 acceptance

- Navigation targets and keyboard/focus behaviour work at supported viewport sizes.
- Exactly one model and one tone are submitted; selecting them makes no provider call.
- GPT-6 Luna default affects new applications only.
- Save/Delete retain their independent safety checks.
- Moving contact actions does not change recipient selection, deletion protection, unlink scope, queueing or mail behaviour.
- Source links, full subject text, Unicode, currency symbols and evidence remain intact.
- Tests are updated alongside changed UI contracts, not loosened simply to make a suite pass.

## Separate operational task — production Gmail readiness

The last reported configuration had credential-presence checks true but all Gmail flags false. Disabled features can cause runtime credential clearing; the UI must distinguish configuration-disabled from missing credentials or authentication failure.

Do not enable sending as part of either development slice. First choose production drafts-only versus drafts-and-sending. Then make a backed-up configuration-only update, restart production, and explicitly verify the intended mailbox before creating any draft or sending email. Do not ask for credential values in chat.

Do not rerun the older Perplexity-enablement utility after Gmail is enabled without revising it: that utility deliberately turns Gmail flags off.

## Milestone status

- Production baseline and local release workflow: established in the preceding work; current live state still requires local verification when deploying.
- Slice 1: planned; recommended next functional slice.
- Slice 2: planned; consolidated review-workspace package.
- Gmail enablement: pending explicit capability choice and mailbox verification.

At each slice completion, update planned/in-progress/verified/released status, record test results and commit ID, and keep production release approval separate from development verification.


## Agreed addition — Assignment evidence library (23 October 2026)

Status: PLANNED. This patch adds the roadmap specification only; no library UI, database, CV ingestion or paid extraction is implemented.

Purpose: Build one comprehensive evidence-backed record for each assignment/contract/role, containing multiple challenge, opportunity, decision and learning scenarios. Reuse approved scenarios for vacancy-specific cover letters, CV proposals and interview preparation.

Assignment overview: separate employer, contracting entity and end client; record title, dates, mandate, authority, starting position, organisational roadmap, delivery landscape, stakeholders, overall contribution and confidentiality.

Scenario fields: situation and business impact; diagnosis and evidence; options considered and trade-offs; personal decision/contribution versus team ownership; actions, techniques and mechanisms with reasons for their selection; tactical intervention; documented strategic objective and connecting mechanism; outcomes with baseline, measure, scope and measurement period; setbacks, adaptations, sustainability and lessons. Link every material claim to a source/version or explicit user confirmation. Contract duration is not delivery duration.

Evidence states: source-supported, user-confirmed, needs clarification, restricted, unsupported. Missing SMART details stay missing. Never transfer outcomes across engagements, infer causation from nearby facts, invent organisational strategy, inflate ownership, or infer current employment. Private evidence stays outside Git/release archives; confidential details must be excluded or anonymised before provider submission. Preserve immutable approved scenario versions.

Outputs: approved short cover-letter paragraphs, concise CV bullet proposals, interview summaries and deeper explanations, follow-up questions covering diagnosis, alternatives, resistance, personal contribution, outcomes and learning. A send is not evidence of ATS submission.

Delivery sequence:
1. Define the assignment/scenario template and evidence/approval rules.
2. Pilot one assignment with source passages and user recollections; flag unanswered questions instead of filling gaps.
3. Validate cover-letter and interview outputs against that record.
4. Populate further assignments in batches.
5. Integrate explicit scenario selection into polishing; send only relevant approved excerpts after existing cost approval.
6. Add interview preparation and evidence-gap views.

Acceptance: correct engagement attribution, traceable approved wording, preserved uncertainty/confidentiality, separate personal/team outcomes and tactical/strategic scope, no paid call on browsing/selecting, no rewriting saved letters/queue/history, no automatic CV update or sending.

# Local production and continuous delivery v1

## Scope
Local workstation production only: development on 127.0.0.1:3000, production on 127.0.0.1:3100, verification on 3200/3201. No LAN/public hosting, Windows service, remote push, automatic GitHub trigger or reboot autostart is installed. Restrict Windows account access to the production folder, especially shared/config. This is explicit tested-commit continuous delivery, not automatic deployment of dirty changes.

## First installation
Stop the current development batch-launcher window. Run from D:\monorepo\NewModularProduct:

    py .\tools\patches\local-production-v1\install.py --apply
    py .\tools\patches\local-production-v1\install.py --check
    py .\tools\deploy\local_delivery.py plan

The installer changes source/tooling only, not Git history, .env or live data. It runs 8 runtime-isolation tests and 18 controller tests with synthetic repositories/databases. The plan command creates a versioned template snapshot under tools/deploy/assets and pins the installed Google-worker dependency closure under tools/deploy/requirements.lock.txt. It creates a JSON plan and readable Markdown review under var/maintenance/delivery. Inspect the listed new/changed files and git diff locally. Do not use git add . . Existing staged work blocks the procedure. Pattern-based scanning is not a guarantee against all private content. Existing unusual tracked files are not silently deleted; private/generated/unrecognised root files are excluded from release extraction.

After reviewing the exact printed plan, run:

    py .\tools\deploy\local_delivery.py checkpoint --plan <printed-plan-json-path>
    py .\tools\deploy\local_delivery.py init --seed
    py .\tools\deploy\local_delivery.py deliver --ref HEAD

Use PowerShell exit-code checks between commands as shown in the accompanying answer. Do not continue after a failure.

Checkpoint tests a separate source snapshot with locked dependency installs, every discovered Node *.test.js file, Python worker tests, controller tests and Playwright browser tests. Only then does it explicitly stage the reviewed paths, remove listed generated bytecode from TRACKING ONLY (local files kept), commit and make an annotated baseline-localprod tag. It never pushes. Real Git hooks are not disabled; detected hook/concurrent scope changes prevent a tested tag and are reported without rewriting history. A failure after staging can leave reviewed paths staged; inspect them rather than reset unrelated work.

Initialisation requires the previously created bootstrap marker. --seed copies the known application/import/outreach databases through SQLite backup + quick_check and copies contacts JSON to production. Stop all other writers; the port check is a guard, not proof that arbitrary external tools stopped. Development originals stay intact. Seeding only works into empty production data and is NOT a later sync mechanism. Omit --seed for deliberately empty production stores. CV inventory is copied to shared/reference; actual CV PDF inputs remain at their configured external location and are not renamed or copied.

Initialisation reads development .env LOCALLY and imports selected provider/candidate configuration into a NEW shared/config/production.env outside Git. It does not print it or change the source .env. All integrations initially OFF. If initialisation fails after a partial copy, inspect it: the tool refuses to overwrite existing state automatically.

Deliver extracts only a committed Git tree. It installs separate dependencies in the release and repeats clean verification against that exact commit, checks health with synthetic state, asks a running production supervisor to pause gracefully, backs up coordinated state and tests candidate startup on a COPY of production state with integrations disabled. Existing schema changes and incompatible declared storage contracts block promotion. Active release metadata switches atomically. Existing data and mail history are never restored/rewound automatically.

## Launch

    D:\NewModularProduct-Production\start-production.bat

Keep that console open. It runs a production-owned supervisor copy, not a mutable development launcher. Production URL:

    http://127.0.0.1:3100/
    http://127.0.0.1:3100/healthz

Health must report production and the promoted commit. If no supervisor was running during deliver, this first launch is required; the promotion command does not claim the app is already running. The original start-local-server.bat remains the DEVELOPMENT launcher and now sets NMP_ENV=development.

Development defaults Gmail and paid integrations OFF, with live credentials cleared while disabled. NMP_ALLOW_DEVELOPMENT_INTEGRATIONS=true is an explicit opt-in for controlled integration testing; do not run development and production against the same real outreach.

After first production health/UI validation, deliberately enable the established flags in production.env and restart the production batch launcher. Credentials/permissions are not changed by deployment. Every Gmail message still needs its established content-specific confirmation. No health check creates a draft or sends mail.

## Subsequent delivery

    py .\tools\deploy\local_delivery.py plan
    # Review the new plan locally, then:
    py .\tools\deploy\local_delivery.py checkpoint --plan <new-plan-json>
    py .\tools\deploy\local_delivery.py deliver --ref HEAD

Developing does not change the running production release. Stop development for full verification because legacy tests may reference port 3000. Production remains available during tests; there is a brief controlled pause for backup/promotion, not zero downtime. With the supervisor running, deliver handles pause/switch/restart/commit-specific health verification. Logs and backups are under shared, outside code releases.

    py .\tools\deploy\local_delivery.py health
    py .\tools\deploy\local_delivery.py status
    py .\tools\deploy\local_delivery.py rollback

Rollback switches CODE to the recorded previous verified release only after contract/schema checks on copied state. It never rewinds Gmail operation history. Future schema changes need a separately reviewed migration and recovery design. A failed/uncertain graceful shutdown does not force-kill the process. Do not blindly delete locks, retry mail operations or restore a historical outreach database after real messages may have been sent.

Failed release directories are retained with candidate.json and a log reference for diagnosis. They are never overwritten automatically. Inspect them before any manual cleanup/retry. A supervisor lock left after a crash similarly requires inspection.

## Dependencies, testing and limits
Node 24+ with SQLite support is required. npm ci uses package-lock.json. A separate Python venv is created in each release; worker dependencies are pinned from the currently installed working closure. Node executable checksum and Python version are verified at production launch. The Python base runtime still belongs to this machine: this is not an OS/container image. Runtime updates require re-verification. Browser/dependency downloads require registry access and the full gates can take several minutes. Failing tests block commits/promotion rather than being bypassed.

The default ignored letter template becomes a reviewed versioned asset. Verification materialises templates/standard-cover-letter.md from that asset for tests; production uses the asset directory. Existing development template settings/data are not replaced.

Offline package evidence: 8 Node tests and 18 Python tests pass; installer syntax/lifecycle/recovery checks pass. Synthetic supervisor IPC is exercised on POSIX. Windows Ctrl+Break handling, real dependency installs, the complete application/browser suite, initial state migration and production startup still require local acceptance. The assistant has not committed the user's repository, deployed a live release or accessed Gmail.
